A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLAM3R study. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SLAM3R reconstruction experiments, component ablations, camera-pose evaluations, and qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and reports additional quantitative reconstruction comparisons and revised camera-pose results.

M1.justification: V3 Section 3.2 newly states that geometric point embeddings are accumulated between adjacent decoder blocks; v1 describes their initial fusion with image features. The PDFs do not establish whether this is an architectural revision or newly disclosed implementation detail. The remaining I2P/L2W architecture, retrieval procedure, and objectives match.

E1.justification: V3 Appendix C adds evaluation on three ScanNet scenes, distinct from the ScanNet++ training dataset. Tanks and Temples and ETH3D receive numerical comparisons but were already evaluated visually in v1. Other dataset and task coverage is retained, including appendix camera-pose and unordered-image reconstruction evaluations.

E2.justification: The pose comparisons drop DIM-SLAM on 7 Scenes and omit native DUSt3R/MASt3R camera estimates, retaining their previously evaluated PnP variants under revised labels (v1 Tables 5–6; v3 Tables 6–7). The principal reconstruction comparator sets remain unchanged. The new MASt3R-SfM citation does not introduce a separately evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The training specification changes substantially: ScanNet++ training plus validation becomes training only, total clips change from 880K to 850K, I2P epoch sampling doubles from 4,000 to 8,000 clips, retrieval training increases from 20 to 50 epochs, and L2W clips change from 13 to 12 frames. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether they reflect reruns or documentation corrections.

E4.justification: V3 adds SLAM3R-NoConf to both pose tables, extending the confidence-filtering comparison to downstream camera accuracy. Existing window-length, alignment, retrieval, scene-frame-count, and MASt3R error analyses are retained. The additional benchmark table is separate from these ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Predicted point-confidence maps are model outputs, not statistical uncertainty reporting for the experimental results.

E6.justification: V3 Table 8 adds quantitative results for nine scenes across three datasets, while the pose tables replace numerous values and add NoConf entries. SLAM3R's reported average ATE changes from 11.27 to 8.41 cm on 7 Scenes and from 7.70 to 6.61 cm on Replica. Main reconstruction and existing ablation scores are retained. Revised training specifications prevent attributing these changes to a controlled same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The pointmap formulations, confidence-aware losses, retrieval objective, and reservoir-sampling mathematics are retained. V3 Appendix B supplies standard formulas for the already-used accuracy, completeness, FPS, and ATE-RMSE metrics; this adds explanation without introducing new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion reframe SLAM3R from a monocular RGB SLAM system to a dense reconstruction system, explicitly emphasizing implicit localization and dense mapping. The central contributions and claims of direct pointmap prediction, reconstruction quality, and 20+ FPS remain.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly acknowledges that derived camera poses fall short of localization-focused SLAM systems. It retains the inability to perform global bundle adjustment but removes v1's explicit limitation concerning accumulated drift in large outdoor scenes. The interpretation that pose accuracy and reconstruction quality need not track each other already appears in v1.

D1.justification: V3 documents inter-block geometric-token accumulation, specifies six scene frames plus six keyframes for L2W training, and expands metric and batch-size documentation. Training-time information is revised. The earlier H100 baseline-hardware disclosure and explicit advertisement of downloadable weights are omitted; actual resource availability cannot be inferred from these omissions.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to ScanNet and MASt3R-SfM and clarifies its relationship to conventional SLAM through the dense-mapping emphasis. The broader survey and positioning relative to DUSt3R and Spann3R are retained.

P1.justification: V3 edits terminology and prose, moves detailed training instructions into Appendix A, promotes pose evaluation into the main text, folds limitations into the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments. Most method exposition and the overall section structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V3 adds the compact pose-summary Table 3 and additional benchmark Table 8, restructures pose-table rows, and relocates existing displays. Captions clarify the existing FPS coloring and default window length. The figures' substantive content and basic two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional quantitative comparisons strengthen generalization evidence that v1 supported largely through visual examples. More explicit implementation details and clearer dense-mapping scope also help readers assess the work. These limited gains outweigh the narrower pose comparisons and removal of the outdoor-drift warning, while the principal reconstruction results remain unchanged.
